reference: Parity cases run procps-ng sysctl (/usr/sbin/sysctl) in the reference Bash and the sysctl builtin in the candidate, both reading only kernel.ostype from the sandbox's read-only /proc. The contract case states the help text directly.
coverage: G84: -b/--binary value output without names or newlines, alone, repeated and after -n; help and synopsis.
exclusions: Writes with -b are not exercised: no sysctl write is made under this safety scope.

cases.purpose: G84: sysctl -b prints a key's value without the 'KEY = ' prefix and without its newline, as procps-ng does (read-only, kernel.ostype).
G84: with several keys, -b output runs the values together with no separator (procps prints 'Linux6.12...').
G84: --binary is the long form, and -b after -n still drops the newline.
cases.script: sysctl --binary kernel.ostype; echo '|'; sysctl -n -b kernel.ostype; echo '|'

cases.purpose: G84: -b is in --help, the help text and the --help usage line.
cases.script:
sysctl --help | grep -c -- '-b, --binary'
help sysctl | grep -c -- '-b/--binary'
sysctl --help | head -n 1
